fields.v: Web-Bench 50 projects x 20 ordered tasks; 31 Skills, 117 core pairs. Conditions: C0 no Skill (baseline), C1 target Skill, C2 length-matched (±5% bytes) irrelevant skip-tier Skill, C3 leave-one-out slice ablation on 5 positive-tail pairs. 4 models. Held constant: workspace, harness, task order, decoding (temperature 0, 64k), Playwright tests; workspace reset (git clean -fdx) before each run. Acceptance tests: Web-Bench Playwright suites. Repetitions: N=3 per cell. Human intervention: none

C1 worse than C0 on all four models: dPass@2 -1.3 to -4.2 pp (3 of 4 CIs exclude zero; GPT-5.1 P@1 CI excludes zero), lower TCD, tokens +72% to +394%; gains on 17-36% of pairs. Losses concentrated on easy tasks (-4.0 to -10.7 pp, CIs exclude zero). Sonnet and Qwen length-distracted, GPT-5.1 and DeepSeek content-misled. Cross-model per-pair correlation |r| ≤ 0.12; 74% of pairs have opposite signs across models. In helpful Skills anti-patterns most cost-effective (p=0.008)

Yes: length-matched control separated two mechanisms a plain C1-C0 comparison would hide; paired bootstrap CIs distinguish model-level effects. Repeatable: N=3; seed spread (Sonnet 4.4 and 3.6 pp across replicates) comparable to headline effect, so pair-level estimates uncertain. Limitations stated: shared C2 prompts (109 unique runs), conservative routing, positive-tail selection for C3 (5 pairs)

Seed variance comparable to effect size; C2 prompts shared across pairs (cluster bootstrap open); only core-tier pairs (no off-target deployment); public high-visibility Skills only; pre-deployment benchmark without live traffic or human interventions; functional correctness only (no visual fidelity, UX, readability); token overhead instead of latency
